International students, 'visa hoppers' and backpackers targeted in Australia migration crackdown
- Published
International students, so-called "visa hoppers" and backpackers will be targeted under stricter rules announced by Australia on Thursday in a bid to curb immigration.
Foreign students will no longer be able to bring their families with them and those who want to extend their stay must choose a higher qualification.
Rules will also be stricter for working holiday visas - commonly used by backpackers and a crucial labour source for the agricultural sector - with a ballot system although these changes will not affect the UK.
The new rules were revealed by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke who said that while immigration was a "strength" of Australia, there needed to be a "high level of control".
For international student and graduate visas, Burke said: "We will no longer be adding to the stock of students automatically being able to bring family members over."
There would be exemptions for foreign students already in Australia as well as applicants from the Pacific and South East Asian countries, he said.
PhD students would also be able to bring their families as they were in different life circumstances to undergraduates, Burke said.
In a speech titled "The work of managing the migration program: who arrives, who stays, who leaves", Burke revealed a raft of changes as the government aims to bring net overseas migration to 225,000 people by 2028.
On student visas, he said the government would clamp down on "visa hopping" - where a student finishes a course, then applies to do another course which is often a lower qualification and sometimes with a "not so legitimate provider".
Students who want to go "up the scale" will be allowed, Burke said, for example, if a student finishes a bachelor's degree and then wants to complete a masters.
He also announced major changes to working holiday visas for those aged 18 to 30 years old who can work in Australia for 12 months, but can extend for a second and third year.
Currently, these visa holders must work for three months in regional Australia during their first year to qualify for a second year, and then six months to qualify for a third year.
Under the new changes, those who qualify for a second year will have to go into a ballot with a cap of 45,000, down from the 57,000 who qualified last year.
For the third year, the ballot will be limited to 5,000, down from 31,000 who qualified last year. British working holidaymakers will not be affected by these changes due to the UK's free trade agreement with Australia.
New figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Thursday showed Australia's population grew 1.4% in the 12 months to March 2026 to 27.9m.
That total figure included births and deaths as well as a net overseas migration of 292,100.
Migration remains a major political issue as debate around Australia's population grows amid rising living costs, housing affordability and increased strain on public services.
One Nation, a populist right-wing party known for its anti-immigration stance and which has seen a surge in support in recent months, detailed its migration policy earlier this week, proposing to cut temporary migrant visas by 750,000 over three years.
The party, which won its first lower house seat in May, also wants to cap net overseas immigration to 130,000, drawing a rebuke from Burke who said such a proposal would risk "smashing parts of the Australian economy".
In July, the government introduced a policy to prioritise applications for family visas lodged onshore - where the applicant is in the country already - over those submitted overseas.
Skilled migrants already in Australia who applied for permanent visas were also prioritised over those applying from overseas.
It also paused applications for working holiday visas from 24 countries, not including the UK.
Violet Roumeliotis, from Settlement Services International which helps new arrivals to Australia, says the migration debate was increasingly driven by "short-term politics rather than what is best for the country".
"The proposed changes to family visas for international students is a good example of this," she said, adding that it would make it harder for Australia to compete for "future talent".

iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.

I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.

Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.

Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27. By the time we publish this post, the update is available for all eligible phones. You can update and test out these new features. Detailed videos of how to use the features are coming soon on our TechPP YouTube channel. If you have any issues or if you don’t find this feature on your iPhone, you can comment below. “First they destroyed our farmland. Then they demolished our homes. Now they are trying to take away our voting rights,” said 74-year-old Sheela Devi, as she stood in front of her jhuggi underneath a bridge near Delhi’s Raj Ghat. The ‘they’ she referred to comprises the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and the state Election Commission. She was one of the over 47 lakh voters left out of Delhi’s draft SIR roll.
One hot afternoon in March 2023, the DDA’s bulldozers tore through standing crop of rice, herbs, and vegetables in Bela Estate after having demolished hundreds of houses of farmers living in the eco-sensitive Zone O floodplains of the Yamuna. The community protested and filed a petition for rehabilitation, but did not get any relief. Their livelihood taken away, the marginalized community has been living since then in tarpaulin covered make-shift shanties under the Geeta Colony bridge and nearby elevated roads.
The slum cluster falls under Part No 38 of Chandni Chowk assembly constituency (Lal Quila Yamuna Bridge). Total 729 enumeration forms were generated as the first step of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise from this Part. The ASDD (Absent-Shifted-Dead-Duplicate) list threw up a shocker as it listed 728 voters, leaving just one name — that of a priest at a local temple — in the draft roll.
In other words, 728 voters out of 729 were excluded from the draft SIR roll — an unprecedented 99.8% deletion rate. The deletions include 42 deaths, and the biggest category is ‘permanently shifted’, which has 632 names. In Chandni Chowk constituency of Old Delhi district, the overall SIR exclusion rate is 38%.
It is deeply ironic that after forcing them to relocate again and again, the State has now moved to strike their names off the electoral roll, marking them as ‘permanently shifted’.
The anxiety now engulfing Sheela Devi and hundreds like her is shaped by what voter-roll deletions have meant for people elsewhere in the country. In West Bengal, for instance, being left out of electoral rolls has been accompanied by questions over citizenship and difficulties accessing government welfare schemes and other entitlements. For a community that has already lost its farmland and homes, the prospect of being deleted from the voter list raises fears that they could be pushed further to the margins, with their identity, access to state benefits and their whole existence called into question.
‘Have Lived here for Generations. This is our Home’
Bela Estate is a large slum cluster on the western bank of the Yamuna, comprising five sub-areas informally known as China Colony, Malla Gaon, Bela Gaon, Moolchand Basti and Kanchan Puri. Residents say the settlement has existed for more than 70 years and is home to over 700 households.
The construction of a bridge in 2009 separated Malla Gaon and China Colony from Bela Gaon, Moolchand Basti and Kanchan Puri. While the latter areas now fall under the Jungpura assembly constituency, Malla Gaon and China Colony are part of Chandni Chowk — and it is here that the mass exclusion of voters occurred during the SIR.
The entire Bela Estate falls within the first phase of the Yamuna Riverfront Development Project, under which the DDA plans to develop a biodiversity park and a lake across 189 acres.
The settlements have faced multiple demolitions over the years. In the months preceding the SIR, residential settlements along the Yamuna floodplains in several parts of Delhi also witnessed a spate of demolitions, carried out by the DDA as anti-encroachment drives.
Among those excluded from Bela Estate are dozens of Sheela Devi’s family members, including her seven sons and their wives. “We have been voting from here for a long time. We have four generations of family here. Our elders lived and died here. We had a house here, we had farmland, everything is gone now,” she said, pointing to a now-grilled boundary that separates the bridge area from the green floodplains.
Janaki Devi (52), standing beside her mother-in-law Sheela Devi, said the booth level officer (BLO) came to give them forms, which they filled and submitted. “We are old voters. I don’t know why we were left out.”
“They can demolish our makeshift houses, but we still stay back here,” she said. “When we could farm, we were fine. Now we hardly get any work. Some in our family are daily-wagers, some others do odd jobs in the market. Some sell vegetables from the cart. Our children have to walk several kilometres to get to the nearest school. But we don’t want to leave. This is our home, we don’t have any village to go back to.”
Octogenarian Ram Charan, who says he arrived here as a toddler with his father, sat on a chaar-payi outside his jhuggi in another cluster of settlements, some distance from where Sheela Devi’s family lives. He cannot walk more than a few meters due to old age, but Ram Charan says he still goes to vote every year. “This is the first time this has happened,” he added.
“We have lived and farmed here in Bela Estate since pre-independence days. Earlier, we had our houses; after those were demolished, we made jhuggis; now we live under these tarpaulin sheets,” the elderly man said, adding, “Since 2004, we have been repeatedly rendered homeless. We have been beaten up by police as well. And now, they have taken away our voting rights.”
“Modi ji had said, ‘Jahan jhuggi wohi makan’. Where is that promise now?” added Pushpa as she came out of her room with her Voter ID card.
A few Jhuggis away, Dulari sits with her friend, chatting. “I have all the documents. I met the BLO here in our settlement, and also provided details of my name from the 2002 voter roll,” she said. Alt News verified her papers and found that her name was indeed there in the last revised list of 2002.
Fifty-five-year-old Kantara Devi, who lay on a chaar-payi, had her midriff bandaged. She cannot sit or walk. She said she fell down amid the chaos and confusion over the draft roll, as people jostled to find out what had gone wrong. “I am worried my widow pension might stop since my name has been struck off. I don’t have any other source of income. That Rs 2,500 is what I live on. I also have to marry my daughter off this month,” she said in a low, broken voice.
The Fight to Prove They Live Here
Kamal Lal, a daily wage worker who is marked ‘permanently shifted’ on the ASDD list, said, “I helped the residents here fill and submit more than 500 enumeration forms. I have taken the BLO to where the voters were residing. She even acknowledged the help I provided. But she said she could not do anything about the exclusions as she was under pressure from higher authorities who wanted to delete votes here. When we went to officials, they said it was DDA’s land and our jhuggi was kachhi (temporary), it won’t be recognised. They asked us whether we had land registration papers, water or electricity bills? I told them there was no rule requiring such documents for voter enumeration.”
Kamal said most people in Bela Estate had their names, or those of immediate relatives, on the 2002 roll. Those who did not have a link to the 2002 roll, had several of the 12 documents listed by the Election Commission, including birth certificates, bank documents and Aadhaar. “We could have been included based on those. But they removed all of us,” he added.
Many residents of Bela Estate belong to the Mallah community (traditional boatmen and fishermen tribes), a notified Scheduled Caste in Delhi, who have been living on the banks of the Yamuna for generations. An ethnographic Census study from 1961 traces the Mallahs as boatmen and fishermen staying in Bela Estate and parts of Mayur Vihar, among other settlements along the Yamuna.
The National Green Tribunal banned vegetable cultivation on the Yamuna floodplain in 2015 citing the river’s toxicity, while the DDA acquired parts of the floodplain for a biodiversity zone and park. In 2019, NEERI found lead levels above FSSAI safety limits in vegetable and soil samples, while a CPCB study flagged fertiliser and pesticide use as a source of pollution. The NGT subsequently ordered the DDA to stop cultivation there. Farmers, however, disputed the findings, saying they primarily used groundwater and manure rather than Yamuna water.
“Our ancestors came here in the 1910s from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and other neighbouring places. The floodplain lands were used during the British times to grow grass for horse grazing. Slowly, people started farming vegetables there. The DDA came much later,” Kamal asserted.
Several families claimed they used to have pucca houses before a 2015 DDA-led demolition. Fearing future demolitions, they stopped trying to build permanent structures and started living in huts and shanties, scattered across the floodplains near Raj Ghat, in the marshes, under bridges, wherever they could find a little space. In the same vain, they never received formal electricity and water connections. Some have gas connections, as this correspondent checked, and use solar batteries to run small fans and lights and charge their phones.
“In this round of SIR, the Election Commission had said that you should only be able to map yourself to the 2002 voter list. And you can show 12 documents including Aadhaar, that should suffice, which they all have,” said Anjali Bharadwaj, a social activist who is the co-convenor of the National Campaign for People’s Right to Information, and founding member of Satark Nagrik Sangathan.
She added, “Their settlements at Bela Estate were broken, and they are living in the same area, But the ERO apparently told them they did not have any proof of electricity and water bills and hence, they can’t be included.”
Deletion Directly Flouts ECI Provisions
According to court submissions during a hearing in August on a petition demanding special provisions for including the homeless and those living precariously in the electoral roll, the counsel for the petitioner argued that since the SIR process “proceeds on the premise that Booth Level Officers would be able to physically locate existing electors at their recorded addresses”, “persons who are homeless or have been rendered homeless or displaced pursuant to demolition drives are at serious risk of systematic exclusion from the electoral rolls, thereby infringing their right to franchise and casting doubt upon their citizenship…”
The court said the ECI’s submission sufficed to address the matter. The counsel for ECI submitted that “there is no requirement to pass a direction as sought by the Petitioner in view of the provisions contained in Manual on Electoral Rolls (“Manual”) published in March, 2023, which provides in Chapter 8 thereof the procedure for determination of ordinary residence.
Clause 8.5 of the manual provides as under:
“Homeless/pavement Dwellers – Homeless/the persons living in sheds/pavement dwellers, who do not possess any documentary proof of ordinary residence are eligible for enrolment in electoral roll, provided they are ordinarily residing there, irrespective of the fact whether that is a private property or pavement or an encroachment on government land. In such case the Booth Level Officer will visit the address given in Form 6 for more than one night to ascertain that the homeless person actually sleeps at the given place…””
The said procedure prescribes such homeless (including those rendered homeless by demolition) persons to fill Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral roll.
When Alt News spoke to sub-district magistrate Manoj Kumar, who is also the electoral registration officer (ERO) of Chandni Chowk, he claimed these voters were excluded because they had moved from their earlier residence. “These people used to do illegal cultivation there. There was a case in 2022 which they lost. After that, the illegal cultivation was stopped. After their houses were demolished, they now stay here and there. In SIR, our BLO visits the registered address. When she did not find them, she marked them on ASDD.”
However, Alt News saw hundreds of copies of enumeration forms which were signed by the BLO upon receipt.
When Alt News called the BLO, Garima Arya, to check whether she could not find the people residing in the area, a woman picked up the phone and claimed it was not Arya’s number. However, residents confirmed the number as belonging to the BLO and the Delhi CEO’s office lists the same phone number for her.
“Just because somebody does not have a residence, that cannot be a ground for remove the name of the person from the voter list,” observed Supantha Sinha, a Supreme Court advocate and member of the Delhi-based citizen’s forum Voter Adhikar Manch.
SDM Kumar also alleged that several voter cards from Bela Estate mentioned ‘agricultural land’ as their address, which Alt News found to be the case, as well. The residents explained that they lived around the land they farmed on and there has never been formal house numbers and streets there, and thus no conventional address.
He also said that his team would set up a camp soon to let the residents submit Form 6 and required declarations for re-enrolling. According to the Manual of Electoral Rolls, they will be registered from the address where they have moved, he added.
When asked whether a person needs proof of residential ownership to be included in the electoral roll, former chief election commissioner Om Prakash Rawat said, “There is no need of property and title. You should not be even asked about these documents because it is not a case of title being judged or checked, and hence proof is to be obtained for that. Electoral roll is for your ordinary residence — that you are ordinarily residing here, that’s good enough.”

By the early 1880s, bacteriology was emerging as a rigorous science. Within the circle of German microbiologist Robert Koch in Berlin, investigators were attempting to isolate specific disease-causing organisms. The logic was to prove that a microbe caused disease, one had to grow it in pure culture, separate it from contaminants, and study its properties systematically. The available solidifying agent was gelatin. It provided a temporary structure to the nutrient broth, allowing colonies to form on the surface. But gelatin was fundamentally flawed: It liquefied at temperatures approaching 37 degrees Celsius, precisely the temperature required to culture many human pathogens. Even worse, several bacteria secreted enzymes that digested gelatin itself. The medium collapsed, colonies merged, and experimental clarity dissolved into formless fluid. For scientists attempting to establish causation of individual species in infectious disease, this was not a minor inconvenience: it was a structural limitation.
Who was Fanny Hesse?
Fanny Angelina Hesse was not formally appointed as a scientist. She assisted her husband, Walther Hesse, who worked in Koch’s laboratory. She prepared materials, maintained cultures, and drew meticulous illustrations of bacterial forms for publication. She was present, not as an investigator, but as a quiet labourer in daily experimental work. It was in that proximity that she repeatedly encountered the gelatin problem. Failed plates, melted surfaces, cultures lost at incubation temperatures. The frustration was practical and persistent. At home, however, she handled another substance entirely. Agar jellies prepared in her kitchen remained firm even in summer warmth. They did not soften as gelatin did. They did not seem to degrade. One evening, in what history records only briefly but imagination can render vividly, the domestic and the scientific converged. The problem of the laboratory and the memory of the kitchen overlapped. She suggested that if agar could withstand heat on the dining table, why would it not withstand incubation in the laboratory?
Before the laboratory
Agar is a complex polysaccharide extracted from the cell walls of certain red algae, mainly species of Gelidium and Gracilaria. Chemically, it consists primarily of two components: agarose and agaropectin. Agarose is a linear polymer made up of repeating units of galactose and 3,6-anhydro-L-galactopyranose, and it is this fraction that gives agar its remarkable gelling property. Agaropectin contains sulfate groups and contributes to viscosity and charge characteristics. The word “agar” is believed to derive from the Malay term agar-agar, meaning jelly.
Long before bacteriologists struggled with melting cultures in Berlin, agar had already lived a quiet life in kitchens. Extracted from red seaweed and known in parts of Asia for nearly two centuries, it was used to set desserts into firm, translucent gels. Unlike gelatin derived from animal tissue, agar did not collapse in warm weather. It held its structure. It was stable. It obeyed heat differently. In the nineteenth century, European cooks encountered agar as an exotic culinary thickener. But in scientific circles, its potential was invisible. The laboratory and the kitchen were separate worlds, divided by sex, habit and hierarchy. No one imagined that a domestic ingredient could resolve a foundational problem in bacteriology.
Thus, Fanny Angelina Hesse’s suggestion to replace gelatin with agar, was out of the box.
Moment of trial
When agar was introduced into nutrient media in Koch’s laboratory, the transformation was immediate and decisive. The medium remained solid at incubation temperatures. It did not liquefy. Most bacteria lacked the enzymatic machinery to degrade it. Colonies appeared as discrete, visible units, each derived from a single organism. For the first time, bacteriologists possessed a surface that was chemically inert, thermally stable, and optically clear. The ability to isolate pure cultures became reliable rather than tentative. Within months, the method was embedded in the experimental practices that led to the identification of the tuberculosis bacillus and other pathogens in the decades to come.
To understand why agar transformed medicine, one must first grasp the idea of culture. A culture medium is an artificial nutrient environment that allows bacteria to grow outside the human body under controlled conditions and at a controlled temperature. Individual bacteria are invisible, but when placed on a suitable medium, such as agar, they form individual visible colonies. This enables laboratories to isolate the exact organism from samples like blood, urine, or sputum. Once identified, the bacteria are tested against different antibiotics to determine which drugs are effective and to detect resistance. Imagine culture is like switching on a floodlight in a dark room. Agar becomes the illuminated stage where hidden microbes step forward, enabling precise diagnosis and rational treatment.
The breakthrough was not dramatic in spectacle. It was a shift merely in material. Yet that shift altered the trajectory of microbiology.
Aftermath and recognition
The scientific practice and literature of the period absorbed agar rapidly, but credit did not travel with equal speed. The technique became standard practice. Petri dishes were designed to accommodate solid media. Textbooks described agar plates as routine apparatus. The name of Koch became synonymous with bacteriological rigour. Fanny Hesse’s contribution receded into footnotes. For decades, the laboratory bench carried her insight without carrying her name. Only later did historians of science begin to recover her role and situate it within the broader narrative of microbiology.
Agar today
More than a century later, agar remains foundational. In every microbiology laboratory, from district hospitals to advanced research institutes, agar plates are prepared daily. Blood agar to detect haemolysis, MacConkey agar to differentiate lactose fermenters, chocolate agar for fastidious organisms. Selective and differential media, all structured upon the same seaweed-derived matrix. Antibiotic susceptibility testing depends on agar diffusion methods. Colony counting for public health surveillance relies on agar surfaces. Molecular biology workflows begin with bacterial colonies grown on agar plates before plasmid extraction or genetic analysis. Even in the era of automated diagnostics and genomic sequencing, agar persists as the primary tool for culturing living microbes.
Today, major production occurs in countries such as Japan, Spain, Chile, China, Indonesia, and Morocco, where seaweed is cultivated or harvested. Beyond microbiology, agar is widely used in the food industry as a vegetarian gelling agent, in confectionery and desserts, in pharmaceuticals as a stabilizer and laxative, and in biotechnology for gel electrophoresis to separate DNA and RNA fragments.
Its properties remain unmatched. It melts at high temperatures but solidifies at lower temperatures, allowing sterile preparation and convenient pouring. It is largely resistant to microbial digestion. It forms a clear, stable gel that supports nutrient supplementation without chemical interference.
Firming up microbiology
Without that transition from gelatin to agar, the systematic isolation of pathogens would have been delayed. The architecture of modern microbiology would have developed more slowly, along a more convoluted path.
Fanny Angelina Hesse recognised continuity between her kitchen and her laboratory. Today, when a microbiologist streaks a plate and waits for colonies to appear, the act is routine. Yet beneath that routine lies the insight of Fanny Hesse. Without her intervention, the discipline might have remained uncertain at its foundation, its cultures unstable, its conclusions tentative.
(Dr. C. Aravinda is an academic and public health physician. The views expressed are personal. aravindaaiimsjr10@hotmail.com)

Mumbai, September 18: The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has revised the registration and distribution process for NCMC cards issued to women, senior citizens and Amrut senior citizens travelling on concession fares.
From September 21, beneficiaries whose fingerprints fail biometric authentication will be able to complete registration using an OTP sent to their Aadhaar-linked mobile number.
The changes are aimed at ensuring that passengers do not lose access to concession fares because of difficulties during biometric verification.
MSRTC has also introduced a replacement facility for NCMC cards that are lost or stolen. From September 21, passengers can block the old card and register for a new one by paying a fee of Rs 199.
QR Receipt Enables Temporary Concession
Passengers who completed NCMC registration by September 19 will be able to collect their cards from September 25. Meanwhile, those registering from September 16 will receive a QR-code-enabled registration receipt.
The receipt can be scanned through the electronic ticketing machine (ETIM) used by ST conductors, allowing eligible passengers to receive concession tickets while they wait for their NCMC card.
The QR receipt will remain valid for 30 days. During this period, beneficiaries must activate their NCMC card and add money to it through a top-up to continue availing the concession without interruption.
Also Watch:
NCMC Made Mandatory From September 1
The NCMC system was made mandatory for women and senior citizens seeking ST fare concessions from September 1. However, technical and registration-related issues had led to difficulties for some beneficiaries.
The latest changes are intended to provide an alternative for passengers facing biometric failures and a temporary digital mechanism until their cards are activated.

Barcelona captain Raphinha said on Friday he hopes to extend his contract at the club and end his playing career there after an explosive start to the season in front of goal.
The Brazil winger has been deployed up front following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and has quickly adapted to the role, scoring 11 goals in seven matches.
“Yes, I intend to extend my contract. When I extended it the first time, I signed until 2028 on the assumption that I would be then 30 or 31 years old, and I didn’t know how things would turn out,” Raphinha told RAC1 radio.
“Given the way I’ve started the season, I think I can keep going for a few more years and I would be very happy to extend my contract and, hopefully, finish my career here without having to go elsewhere,” the 29-year-old added.
ALSO READ: Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal says he experiences racism ‘a thousand times’
Raphinha was appointed captain at the start of the season after Ronald Araujo and Marc-Andre ter Stegen left the club and Frenkie de Jong was sidelined by a knee injury.
The former Leeds United forward joined Barcelona in 2022, but Flick’s arrival as coach two years later proved a turning point for both the team and Raphinha, who had become increasingly frustrated under Xavi Hernandez.
He has now scored 86 goals in 184 appearances for Barcelona, 66 of them under Flick, who has led the Catalans to La Liga titles in each of his two seasons.
Raphinha netted a hat-trick in Wednesday’s 7-2 win over Racing Santander as Barcelona maintained its perfect record this term, having won all seven matches, including a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord in its Champions League opener.
Barcelona sits three points clear of Real Madrid and Real Betis ahead of Saturday’s trip to fifth-placed Sevilla.

Will England boss Tuchel 'embrace the chaos'?
- Published
England manager Thomas Tuchel left the United States in July pining for greater control.
At his first squad announcement since the World Cup on Friday, the German spoke of "embracing the chaos".
Is it possible to have controlled chaos? It seems Tuchel is ready to find out.
England's third-placed finish in the US was the nation's best performance at the World Cup since 1966.
But the memories of the team's semi-final loss to Argentina linger.
In the aftermath of the heartbreaking defeat, Tuchel pointed to his team's inability to find control having taken the lead via Anthony Gordon's opener as a key factor behind his side's late collapse.
Fast-forward two months, however, and the messaging is rather different ahead of the four upcoming Nations League games.
"Football is about adapting to situations and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach, if you look at the 6-4 against France [in the World Cup bronze-medal match]," said Tuchel.
"But people talk about it like it's one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match, so maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best."
- Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning 
  - Published2 hours ago
Mixed signals? Or maybe it is just a sign that Tuchel wants his side to become more unpredictable in their search for success.
Because that is what the best teams do - mix it up when required.
Despite Tuchel's remarks, his latest squad for the fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia rather contradicts any thoughts of a havoc-rich approach.
The return of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer, two of English football's most technically gifted players, screams control.
So do the call-ups of Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, who are both extremely adept in possession of the ball.
Of course, there is certainly a balance to be struck. That would be Tuchel's ideal scenario.
Rio Ngumoha's first senior call-up will certainly add an air of unpredictability to Tuchel's options.
The Liverpool winger, 18, has had an exciting start to the season, catching the eye with his invention and trickery down both flanks for Andoni Iraola's side.
That Tuchel revealed Fulham attacker Josh King is also close to earning his first senior call-up provides further indication the England manager wants to reinvigorate his forward line ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign and beyond.
Yet, we shouldn't expect Tuchel to completely let go of the handbrake just yet.
In response to a question as to whether his team can replicate the fast-paced approach of a Premier League team but harnessed with a greater control, Tuchel responded: "That would be the wish, that we become for 10 minutes a little bit more like Spain, here and there.
"The more I reflect on it, it's maybe more buying into our strengths and play more minutes like we played the second half against Croatia, and more minutes like we played the first half against France, and buying into these strengths, because I think we get a lot of value out of it, we get a lot of connection to the fans, this is what the Premier League reflects.
"We are maybe not the most economical team to play football but this is maybe also a characteristic of the Premier League. The Premier League is not a very economical league, you have to play.
"You need to max out every single match otherwise you cannot compete for the title so this is something more beautiful. But this is where we are, where I am in my mindset and I think where the players are, so it's still a bit ambiguous."
But while Tuchel may not have total clarity with regards to whether control or chaos is the way forward, he showed no hint of confusion over who he believes his best players are.
Tuchel refuted assertions his decision to recall Palmer and Alexander-Arnold was an admission he'd got his World Cup squad wrong.
Indeed, Tuchel has hinted he would have picked a vastly similar squad for the upcoming games to the one he selected for the US had all his options been available.
"Before we did the nomination in the last month, I thought we had more of a continuation of the World Cup squad but then a lot of members of our World Cup squad - Reece [James], Dan [Burn], Dean [Henderson, [John] Stones, [Jordan] Henderson, Djed Spence - can't be with us due to injuries, so it is not like a full continuation.
"These players were crucial for us in building the brotherhood, in building the spirit and taking care of the mentality that took us the long way in the tournament. We will not negotiate on that, we will not give in on that.
"So other players will step up, this is basically how I see this camp.
"My mindset at the moment is not to change too much within the formations."

It was at the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona when the mutterings about a new "secret weapon" started.
Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance – a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.
They were talking about creatine.
Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.
But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' – even if it was legal.
From the minute an athlete wakes, to the moment they go to bed, they are thinking about how they can optimise their performance and recovery.
Today, creatine is just one of a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in this pursuit of marginal gains. Some help with muscle size and strength, while others correct deficiencies in the diet.
"There are various reports in the literature of some studies that say maybe up to 90% of athletes take supplements. I often jokingly say that means 10% are lying," says Prof Graeme Close, professor of human physiology at Liverpool John Moores University.
"The sports teams that I've worked in, I think that's probably closer to 100% of athletes will be taking some form of supplementation."
So, what do supplements actually do and why do athletes take them? And in the world of strict liability, where elite athletes are solely responsible for what they put in their bodies, how do they make sure they stay clean?
While experts like Close advocate for seeking to meet nutritional needs through food in the first instance, it may not always be possible or practical to do this - and that is where supplements come in.
Take, for example, creatine, which is found naturally in meat and fish.
"You would need the best part of a kilogram of raw chicken a day to get the amount of creatine you need," says Close. But it is unsafe to eat raw poultry because of the food poisoning risk from harmful bacteria.
Creatine is a natural compound in the body produced in the kidneys, liver and pancreas. It is a quick source of energy for muscles, which is especially important for short-duration, high intensity activities such as sprinting.
Its big break as a supplement came in the 1990s when two scientists who had been researching it for two decades shared their findings with Steve Jennings, whose Maxim sports nutrition company supplied products to the British Olympic team.
During the 1992 Barcelona Games, investigative reporter Doug Gillon had learned of a 'secret trial' involving British athletes and seen a box of their Ergomax C150 – effervescent creatine tablets. He wrote that if the scientists' claims - that creatine could improve explosive athletic performance by 1-3% - were true, then "sport may never be the same again".
In terms of sport supplements and nutrition, he was right. By the time of the next Olympics in 1996, an estimated 80% of athletes were taking creatine, and since then it has become mainstream, with research suggesting there may be cognitive benefits as well as physical.
According to the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, the creatine breakthrough of the 1990s had "launched a new era in sports nutrition" and "sparked exploration into other supplements".
The global dietary supplements market size was valued at $209.5bn (£154bn) in 2025 and is projected to grow to $431.7bn (£317.4bn) by 2033, according to Grand View Research., external
Close, who oversaw nutrition for last year's British and Irish Lions rugby union tour, sees supplements as the "final piece of the jigsaw" rather than a starting point.
"What we're talking about is small margins of benefit, where actually these athletes who focus on the food, I think what you often find is that they've got the big-ticket items right," he says.
"So they're seeing great performance benefits because their overall diet is immaculate.
"They might be missing out on the one per-centers, but they've really nailed the 99 per-centers. And they often do better than those who chase the one per-centers but have not given enough attention to the 99 per-centers."
Australian cyclist Nicole Frain agrees, adding: "I'm a pretty big believer that they are called sport supplements. They are there to supplement the things you already do right.
"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.
"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating – all of those things – before we add in all of the extras."
Close puts protein powders top of the list of supplements taken by athletes he works with, followed by creatine and vitamin D.
Protein powders maximise muscle repair and contribute to muscle growth, while creatine is a quick source of energy for muscles and important in short-duration, high-intensity activities like sprinting. Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for bone health and supports muscle function.
Other popular supplements include carbohydrate gels, which Close says were key in the first sub-two hour marathon run earlier this year by Kenyan long-distance runner Sabastian Sawe.
"As sport nutritionists we were all fascinated at what the fuelling programme was, and it was the sports drinks and gels that played a huge part of that fuelling," Close says.
"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.
"And the reports coming out of the recent sub-two-hour marathon was that it was 110 grams of carbohydrate per hour that was achieved."
Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.
So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?
"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.
"So just because something enhances performance, if it's not dangerous to health and not against the spirit of sport, Wada will not touch it.
"So creatine is a good example.
"Though something like an anabolic steroid, where it's against the spirit of sport to be injecting yourself for a performance benefit, it's dangerous to health and it's performance enhancing - that hits all three."
But taking a supplement still carries anti-doping risks.
"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.
And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.
There are supplement-testing programmes which batch test products before they are sold to make sure they do not contain any Wada-prohibited substances.
One of those is Informed Sport, which says as many as one in 10 supplements is contaminated with ingredients and compounds prohibited in sport and points to a study carried out by the Anti-Doping Knowledge Centre that showed product contamination was responsible for 8% of all anti-doping violations between 2005 and 2022.
While Informed Sport is a very well used system among athletes, Wada makes it clear that quality assurance schemes can reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an anti-doping infringement.
If you do accept the risk, you need to be organised to keep track.
In the case of Great Britain rower Heidi Long, it takes a spreadsheet.
"I've recorded the batch number of every product that I've taken and its expiry date because if you take it after the expiry date the Informed Sport [certification] is no longer viable," she says.
Close says he has also done site visits to factories to see where the supplements are made to check the manufacturing processes because "the risk of failing a drugs test is huge".
There are risks to the general population too, he adds, saying: "You can be buying supplements off the internet that are made in somebody's garage and you've got no idea of the manufacturing processes."
He points to studies on creatine products which have found there is no creatine in them and so "you're completely wasting your money" and that in the worst case scenario it may contain substances that are dangerous to your health.
"So it is really important that the message is that while they can play a small role, the safety considerations are the key factor," he says.
There is, however, more than one way for an elite athlete to chase a competitive edge – and some are going back to basics.
For every trending supplement, there is an unprocessed, wholefood alternative – from the anti-inflammatory benefits of turmeric, staving off cramp with pickle juice or consumption of high-nitrate foods like beetroot before competition.
It is what Close calls a "food-first" or "food-only" approach and something he says every athlete should use as a starting point.
The latest to have its moment in the spotlight is an ancient Ethiopian grain called teff.
Used for thousands of years in traditional east African diets, teff is now making its mark globally in performance nutrition.
In comparison to other popular grains like wheat, rice and quinoa, teff has a high mineral content and is rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C. Naturally gluten-free and good for the gut, it is also unique for being a 'complete' protein, meaning it provides all nine essential amino acids required for human nutrition.
These superfood credentials have caught the attention of some of the world's best athletes over the years, from Olympic champion marathon runner Haile Gebrselassie to seven-time Grand Slam singles champion Venus Williams, and it is now becoming a more common sight on UK supermarket shelves.
British boxer Fran Hennessy was introduced to teff by her nutritionist and it is now part of her daily routine.
"I've never looked back," she says. "What I'm putting in my body is good fuel and energy and teff has so much. It energises you so much before a workout and it gives you the fibre you need."
As well as boosting her performances, Hennessy credits teff with being key to recovery.
She says: "Each meal I'm having there's a reason behind and everything that's in it there's a reason behind... I know what I'm putting in my body is fuelling me, recovering me, energising me."
Cost is another consideration when athletes are deciding on supplements.
"The supplement industry is really expensive," says Long. "And we're definitely not made of money. So I think it's really picking and choosing when you want to put that investment in."
She says it makes sense to have more supplements around racing time "when the performance is super critical and very time dependent".
"[But] on a daily basis if I can get the protein intake from my dinner and a glass of milk or yoghurt and breakfast then actually I was going to be eating that food anyway so it's not as expensive."
And then there is taste.
"I would much rather enjoy a coffee in the morning with friends or while I'm working rather than have one of the gels," she says. "Some of the gels ... you'll end up holding your nose when you take it.
"I guess it's just like the enjoyment of what you're taking, you know, it's nicer to eat food than it is to take supplements."

Data center developer sues city after requiring company to supply renewable energy on-site
Critics of the data center in St. Louis, Missouri, worry about its water usage, the impact on the city’s air quality and utility costs
The developer of a proposed $3.1 billion data center in St. Louis, Missouri, has sued a board that handles city zoning after the five-member panel required the company to supply renewable energy on-site.
David Lambiaso, a partner at data center developer TerraWatt, claimed in a lawsuit filed Wednesday that the St. Louis Board of Adjustment imposed illegal conditions when it upheld a permit for the 120-megawatt facility in July, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, which reported on the filing.
The lawsuit argues that requiring his company to supply a minimum of 2.4 megawatts of renewable energy at the data center exceeds the board’s authority.
The rapid development of data centers across the country to power the AI boom has often led to friction between cities and developers, with locals citing environmental and quality of life concerns.
Some St. Louis residents have complained that the proposed data center in the Midtown neighborhood would use too much water, worsen air quality and raise utility costs, the Post-Dispatch reported.
Lambiaso also claimed the renewable energy requirement is “practically impossible” given the size of the 11-acre site.
The Independent has reached out to TerraWatt and the St. Louis City Counselor’s Office for comment.
TerraWatt did agree to use renewable energy for at least 50 percent of the data center’s energy load within five years of the facility’s opening in a community benefits agreement.
That amounts to about 60 megawatts — far more than the 2.4 megawatts mandated by the board. But there are other ways to generate that energy, rather than producing it on site, such as buying power from energy providers.
Local environmentalists have argued the community benefits agreement does not actually represent residents’ wishes.
Elyse Schaeffer with the Missouri Coalition for the Environment told local outlet KSDK, “I'm reluctant to call this a community benefits agreement at all because at base level a community benefits agreement should involve conversations with feedback from and input by community members. And that's not the process that we saw happen with this.”
“‘Community Benefit Agreement’ — which community does it benefit? It should be called a Developers' Benefit Agreement,” Kerry McCullen with the Eco-Socialist Green Party of Eastern Missouri told the outlet. “The community did not and does not consent to this. It is being forced upon us. It's disgusting that we have no say in the matter.”
The St. Louis Board of Adjustment has also required aldermen to approve the community benefits agreement, which Lambiaso argued in the lawsuit exceeds the board and aldermen’s authority.
